content.comment_body: Hello, I am attempting to connect a [product_name] device to a Micro850 PLC using Modbus TCP. I need the [product_name] to read the holding registers from the Micro850 PLC. Is this connection possible, and how can I verify the values read within the [product_name]? I'm new to this type of device. Thank you for your assistance.

Hello [user_name], and welcome to the forum. Yes, you can establish a Modbus TCP/IP connection between a [product_name] and a Micro850 PLC. Please note, however, that not every [product_name] supports Modbus TCP/IP. Only devices with specific [article_no] and firmware levels (such as FS4 or higher, or recent hardware revisions) support this protocol. The [product_name] handles only integer values in the range of -32,768 to 32,767, which can be read via an analog network input. For floating point or double floating point values, you will need to use a "Float/Integer converter" block to process and display them.

Thank you for the warm welcome and your quick response. We are actually using a device with [article_no]. I will review the [document] you've provided and attempt communications between the devices. If it works, I'll update this thread; if I encounter issues, I may ask for further advice. I appreciate your help.
We're looking forward to your next update or question.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants discussed connecting a [company_name] automation device to a Micro850 PLC by Modbus TCP, emphasizing the importance of hardware compatibility and understanding the data format constraints. The support for Modbus TCP/IP is conditional on device model and firmware version. Users must verify both device selection and proper data type handling—especially for converting integers and floating point values when gathering data from external sources.
